notToBeConfusedWith.name: Bitter orange
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Seville and its relatives are too sour to eat and are grown for marmalade, liqueur and peel; a recipe calling for orange means the sweet kind unless it says otherwise.

forms.label: Sweet, whole
forms.sourceNote: Oranges, raw, navels. Public domain. One orange is the record's own 2 7/8 inch fruit portion. No density is carried: an orange is not poured, and where a recipe uses only the peel the line states how little of the fruit reaches the drink.
